# [STORY] As a maintainer, I want the frontend build to be audit-clean and CI-green, so that the app ships with no known moderate+ vulnerabilities

## User Story
**As a** maintainer
**I want** the frontend dependency tree to pass `npm audit --audit-level=moderate` and the CI pipeline to be fully green
**So that** the app ships with no known exploitable vulnerabilities and every merge is gated by a passing build

## Parent Epic
Parent: #121

## Acceptance Criteria (Given/When/Then)
- [x] Given the remediated dependency tree, when `npm audit --audit-level=moderate` is run, then it exits 0.
- [x] Given the frontend CI workflow, when a push triggers it, then lint, test, and build steps all pass.
- [x] Given the frontend CI workflow, when `npm audit --audit-level=high` runs as a CI gate, then it exits 0. (Implemented as `--audit-level=moderate` instead — strictly stricter, so a pass at moderate is also a pass at high. Rescoped to match what #131 actually shipped.)
- [x] Given the test suite after migration, when `npm test -- --coverage` is run, then coverage meets the 80% threshold.

## Definition of Ready
- [x] Meets [Definition of Ready](https://github.com/liviuionesi/lmdb.dev/blob/develop/docs/process/DEFINITION_OF_READY.md)

## Notes
Closed via #131 (commit ec9c006 on develop). `npm audit` is 0 vulnerabilities at every severity (not just above the moderate bar). CI's audit gate uses `--audit-level=moderate`, a strictly stricter check than this story's original `--audit-level=high` wording, so that AC is satisfied by the stronger implementation rather than the literal flag.

One known, tracked gap: 2 tests in `media.test.js` are skipped (pre-existing jsdom hang, unrelated to this story's changes) — tracked separately in #132, which doesn't block this story's DoD since the underlying dependency/CI work this story covers is fully done and verified.
